expect.why: the block committed at 02 is still the first block at 03, byte for byte, and the second is appended under it; passages append, and appending is what the rule permits
each witness digests to its own section as the commit before its own lift held it, and each held passage is a contiguous run of that section
both lifts left their citing sentence in the section it was in — the Observation's at commit 02 and the Method's at commit 03
each lift moved the section it took prose out of, and each is discharged by the reading verdict written in the same commit

note: the near-negative of D70 and D72, and the second half of what K31 cannot show: there, the entry held no passage before the lift, so the append-only comparison had an empty list on one side and could not tell appending from anything else. Here a committed block is still there, unchanged, with a second one under it. An entry accumulates passages the way it accumulates verdicts, one per lift, and a project that lifts twice out of one artifact is the ordinary case rather than the strange one.
history: apply commits/01, commits/02, … as successive commits in a fresh repository; expectations name the commit they apply to. `@commitNN` in an entry is substituted with the real short object id of that commit before it is made, because a seed cannot know an id the runner has not created yet
